Should a venture firm lead Truna's ~$15M seed on manufactured decision experience?

14 September 2026, 15:22 IST· 8 findings that reprice the thesis · 20 premises disproved · 247 other ways to build it
The answer, and what it rests on
the finding

Fund the kill experiments, not the round

The $15M round as proposed does not clear. 73% of the 561 evidence items came back inconclusive, because every company-specific claim rests on the deck: a public footprint 19 days old, no incorporation record, founders unverifiable. The blind-scored decomposition experiment is real progress — training closes 58% of the gap to a 27B reference against 32% from worked examples — but the training line is undisclosed across a stated ten-fold range, the $11.5M compute line names no pricing basis, and no fine-tuned capability on record has held margin across three frontier releases.

What survives is smaller and staged. Of 247 venture shapes generated, 22 reached decision depth, and the strongest is a $2-3M pre-round instrument funding the decisive tests before anyone prices the company: the verifier error curve, a measurement one run answers, and the remaining recipe work gated on rate of progress across attempts, custodian-scored within 14 weeks and converting at a 25-40% discount on pass. Beside it sit decision-experience context packs productising the arm that already works, and a hybrid cheque of $6-8M equity with compute assembled through credits and reserved capacity rather than bought at dilution prices.

The three findings that move it most

Of eight that reprice the thesis. Each changes a specific number in the case rather than an impression of it.

1
Settles, in training's favour, the baseline whose absence was the stated reason not to price the round: on the decomposition step, worked examples close 32% of the 2.33-point gap to a 27B reference while training closes 58%. It leaves the cost question — whether the budget buys enough attempts — exactly as open as before.

A 27B reference, an untuned 2.1B, and the same 2.1B tuned on 115,580 decomposition problems drawn from 259 existing plans were scored in one blind pass over 37 held-out cases at 0, 1, 2, 10 and 100 worked examples. No example count reaches the tuned model's empty-prompt score of 7.28; the untuned model gains 0.75 from its first example then falls to 5.52 at a hundred, below its 5.93 start, and the 27B given the same examples gains 0.11 at best. On whether the dividing line falls somewhere real, examples make the untuned model monotonically worse (4.89 to 3.32) while the tuned model holds near 6.30. Blind-scored by an independent judge with retained transcripts; company-run, single judge, and the step-level retrieval arm a sceptic would ask for has not been run.

Source: Truna internal blind evaluation of the decomposition step (unpublished)

2
The '100 to 1,000 times above market' multiple on the training line is void; what replaces it is an undisclosed cost structure spanning a stated ten-fold range, and the non-disclosure is itself the finding.

The evidence prices fine-tuning at $40 to $30,000 per run from generic vendor cost-calculator and comparison pages, at confidence 0.1, and itself admits the estimates were synthesised from Wikipedia cost data and general industry knowledge. That prices a single low-rank adapter on an existing base, not what this training line must buy: multiple adapters plus a ranking head, two-phase hidden-state distillation, a preference-ranking objective, matched-size ablations across two domains, and retraining every two to four months. The line funds an unknown number of experimental attempts, not one production run, so no per-sequence figure derived from it is valid. Base model size, full fine-tuning versus adapters, ablation count and GPU pricing basis are all undisclosed.

Source: Fine-Tuning Cost Calculator — AI Cost

3
If the $11.5M compute line was quoted at on-demand rates, the same capacity at three-year reserved pricing costs roughly $4.6M to $6.9M — a potential overstatement of several million dollars in a $15M ask. The pricing basis and quote date are stated nowhere.

No public source states whether the $11.5M compute line assumes spot, on-demand, reserved or credited pricing, or when it was quoted. AWS three-year reserved instances discount up to 72% off on-demand rates and Google Cloud three-year committed-use discounts reach 70%; at a 40-60% discount, an on-demand-quoted $11.5M becomes roughly $4.6M to $6.9M at reserved pricing. The month-by-month drawdown plan and the fraction committed in the first six months are equally undisclosed, and the line has not been decomposed into named experiments with capacity requirements. Nearly a third of the raise therefore rests on an unstated pricing assumption.

Source: AWS EC2 Reserved Instances Pricing

Eight findings that reprice the thesis

Each was produced by a web-grounded investigation, and each changes a specific number in the investment case. The headline is the conclusion; open a row for the evidence.

▶Settles, in training's favour, the baseline whose absence was the stated reason not to price the round: on the decomposition step, worked examples close 32% of the 2.33-point gap to a 27B reference while training closes 58%. It leaves the cost question — whether the budget buys enough attempts — exactly as open as before.1 / 8

On whether the dividing line falls somewhere real, examples make the untuned model monotonically worse (4.89 to 3.32) while the tuned model holds near 6.30. Blind-scored by an independent judge with retained transcripts; company-run, single judge, and the step-level retrieval arm a sceptic would ask for has not been run.

Source: Truna internal blind evaluation of the decomposition step (unpublished)

That prices a single low-rank adapter on an existing base, not what this training line must buy: multiple adapters plus a ranking head, two-phase hidden-state distillation, a preference-ranking objective, matched-size ablations across two domains, and retraining every two to four months. The line funds an unknown number of experimental attempts, not one production run, so no per-sequence figure derived from it is valid. Base model size, full fine-tuning versus adapters, ablation count and GPU pricing basis are all undisclosed.

Source: Fine-Tuning Cost Calculator — AI Cost

▶If the $11.5M compute line was quoted at on-demand rates, the same capacity at three-year reserved pricing costs roughly $4.6M to $6.9M — a potential overstatement of several million dollars in a $15M ask. The pricing basis and quote date are stated nowhere.3 / 8

No public source states whether the $11.5M compute line assumes spot, on-demand, reserved or credited pricing, or when it was quoted. AWS three-year reserved instances discount up to 72% off on-demand rates and Google Cloud three-year committed-use discounts reach 70%; at a 40-60% discount, an on-demand-quoted $11.5M becomes roughly $4.6M to $6.9M at reserved pricing. The month-by-month drawdown plan and the fraction committed in the first six months are equally undisclosed, and the line has not been decomposed into named experiments with capacity requirements. Nearly a third of the raise therefore rests on an unstated pricing assumption.

Source: AWS EC2 Reserved Instances Pricing

▶The claim that the competitive window is open and unoccupied — a load-bearing element of the venture premium — was reached without searching the relevant literature and must be restated as bounded by what was searched. At least seven named published lines of work occupy the mechanism.4 / 8

The mechanism the company calls 'latent state' is an active published field under the names latent reasoning, continuous thought and implicit chain-of-thought: Coconut (Meta/FAIR, ICLR 2025), Quiet-STaR, CODI, pause tokens and recurrent-depth approaches all carry reasoning in hidden states without serialising steps into tokens. None was retrieved by the searches that concluded no group is entering this space, because those searches used the phrase 'latent state', which returns state-space models and POMDPs instead. BDH-CQ (arXiv 2608.09888, independently audited) already reaches 29.5% pass@2 on ARC-AGI-1 with a 150M-parameter model reasoning entirely in recurrent latent space, at $0.0007 per task — roughly 57 times cheaper than GPT 5.6 Luna.

Source: BDH-CQ: In-Context Learning with Recurrent Latent Reasoning

▶Trained weights must be priced as a recurring cost centre, not a durable asset: the documented base rate for a fine-tuned advantage surviving three frontier releases is zero, and calibration must be re-earned at each two-to-four-month retraining the plan already assumes.5 / 8

No documented case exists of a fine-tuned procedural capability — code assistant, translation engine, domain agent — that sustained commercial margin across three or more frontier model releases. The products that survived, such as Copilot and Cursor, swap base models underneath rather than fine-tune, and OpenAI shut its self-serve fine-tuning platform in May 2026. Separately, five peer-reviewed papers from 2025-2026 show calibration does not survive base-model swaps or fine-tuning changes, so the value-of-information ranking the product depends on must be recalibrated at every retraining cycle, a cycle the plan itself sets at every two to four months as base models turn over.

Source: OpenAI Shutting Down Fine-Tuning Signals for Enterprise AI

▶Every company-specific number in the case — partner engagements, demonstration results, budget lines — is verifiable from no source outside the deck, so the cost of primary verification and escrowed proof belongs in the price of the round.6 / 8

The truna.ai domain was registered on 2026-08-24, nineteen days before the third-party diligence study dated 2026-09-12, with the registrant hidden behind a proxy. No incorporation record exists in India's MCA registry, Delaware, or any other searched jurisdiction, and the deck itself states 'legal form is to be confirmed'. Founder identities are unverified from public sources, which makes IP chain-of-title checks impossible. Across roughly 1,500 searches and 2,000 pages, zero independent discourse about the company was found: no Crunchbase profile, no LinkedIn page, no press, no third-party commentary. The three design-partner engagements and the five demonstrations rest on the deck alone.

Source: WHOIS — truna.ai

▶The external-custody structure the evaluation-credibility plan depends on has no institution able to execute it: the month-six custody milestone and the six-to-ten-week metric-ratification window are not achievable as scheduled, which reprices the $2.5M sealed-evaluation line and the readout timetable.7 / 8

As of September 2026 no credible, conflict-free institution exists to hold sealed decision-worlds and blind-score regret against cost. Big Four firms sell AI assurance without sealed-enclave evaluation infrastructure, the AI safety institutes hold a public-safety mandate rather than a commercial benchmarking one, evaluation startups carry conflicts with the frontier labs they serve, and academic protocols such as TRUCE are not operational. Nor can any external body ratify the metric definition on the plan's timeline: ISO's fastest standard development takes about three years, and MLCommons and IEEE operate on multi-month to multi-year cycles against a six-to-ten-week window with zero float. Standard escrow terms run twelve months, against a multi-year custody need.

Source: AEF-1 Minimum Operating Conditions for Independent Third-Party AI Evaluations

▶Raises the expected number of experimental attempts the undisclosed training budget must cover, and converts the training gate from a one-shot measurement into a search that must be judged on rate of progress across attempts, with an abandonment condition stated in advance.8 / 8

Eight peer-reviewed studies from 2023 to 2026 show that generation, ranking and calibration objectives interfere when trained jointly on mid-size models: roughly 32% gradient-conflict incidence, an average 1.5-point loss against single-task training, CAPO (ACL 2026) proving reinforcement-learning gradients for accuracy misalign with calibration, and JGR (ACL 2023) finding generation and ranking pull in opposite directions. This is the exact objective mix the training line must buy. A recipe that fails on early attempts has shown little, since a later attempt may succeed; the valid gate for this work is progress rate across attempts, not a single pass-or-fail run, and only genuine measurements — such as whether the verifier error curve holds at depth — may be gated on a pre-registered outcome.

Source: CAPO: Calibration-Aware Policy Optimization

Premises the study disproved

20 assumptions have been carried into the analysis and then invalidated against evidence. The 6 with the largest consequences are below. Confidence is the post-investigation figure — the lower it is, the harder the premise failed.

Conf.Premise that failedWhat the evidence showed
0.15The compute buyer's market persists through the 18-24 month deployment window, so the generation and training budgets are priced against falling GPU prices and courting counterparties.The evidence points the other way. Every prior GPU cycle reversed on a demand shock, discounted capacity is preemptible with no availability guarantee, and reserved capacity is sold against enterprise-scale commitments a seed budget does not reach. A mid-window tightening leaves the remaining budget buying materially less than planned.
0.15Decision-makers can and will absorb the deliverables at their natural size: 92 considerations, a 1,587-package interlocking plan.The demonstrations measure coverage and impact of what was generated, never human uptake of it. Decision science consistently finds long analytical artifacts are skimmed and top-sliced. If real consumption is a thin slice, the sellable layer is the ranking, not the completeness the training thesis is built on.
0.18Independent grading of 20-30 decisions completes inside months 1-5 on a thirty-person fractional panel coordinated by founders running six concurrent workstreams.The gate runs on practitioner calendars and grading-protocol iteration, not compute. Comparable expert panels with dedicated professional staff have taken far longer than five months, and fractional scheduling adds delay. A six-to-nine-month grading cycle slips the readout a full frontier-release interval regardless of engineering progress.
0.20In a kill branch the generated material, the generator and the benchmark instrument are marketable assets recovering 0.4-0.6x, rather than orphaned IP.The named buyers state the opposite preference: data marketplaces prioritise real operational records over synthetic sets, and no laboratory expression of interest, letter of intent, or price signal for decision-experience material was found. A failed readout devalues the asset at exactly the moment the sale would occur.
0.25The consistency-verification pipeline holds a false-accept rate low enough at 100,000-sequence scale that label noise does not swamp the training signal.Published production data shows a small specialist verifier catching roughly one error in five, in-loop verifier metrics read five to ten times optimistic, and verifier and generator failures are not independent when both encode the same makers' modelling choices. No error-rate measurement exists for this pipeline at any scale.
0.30The five demonstrations constitute substantially independent lines of evidence, so the investment memo may count three measured demonstrations as cumulative support.One maker, one grading apparatus and no external custody mean instrument failure modes propagate to all five at once, and peer-reviewed work shows shared infrastructure induces correlated failures between generator and judge. Counted honestly, the demonstrations are one correlated observation, not cumulative support.

What survives, in five families

22 shapes have reached decision depth with quantified success criteria; 22 of them are grouped below into five theses about where value actually sits. The blue line under each shape is the study's own success threshold, not an estimate laid on top of it.

Sell the experience, not the training4 shapes

The strongest measured result is the third demonstration: ~1,000 generated sequences supplied as context to a frontier model produced 92 exclusive high-impact considerations. That output is sellable without the ~$6M training claim, and it improves with every frontier release instead of decaying against one. These shapes package generated decision experience as context packs, rehearsal environments and private pre-check surfaces, deferring the weights question entirely.

Sell manufactured decision experience as context packs — no training claim, no training spend
Context packs sustain >=2x exclusive high-impact considerations vs bare frontier baseline across two consecutive frontier releases
Decision simulators: sell Truna-generated worlds as rehearsal environments for executive teams and AI agents
The drill, not the prediction, is the product — sufficiency need only hold within Truna-generated worlds
The executive pre-check seat: a confidential personal rehearsal surface, sold per-seat, excluded from the company record by default
5 sponsor executives using the seat weekly within 3 months of offer
Sell discovery to diligence buyers4 shapes

Funds, lenders and insurers already pay $50-250k per deal for exactly what blind discovery produces: the mechanism the deck omitted. The buying trigger recurs weekly, outcomes are dated and recorded, and the product needs no trained model. These shapes package machine-run discovery as fixed-fee engagements sold into existing diligence and assurance budget lines, with the self-diligence run as the demonstration.

Risk Register Gap Audit: score a capital programme's risk register against a machine-built decision space, fixed fee, two weeks
A material, customer-acknowledged register omission found in >= 70% of audits
The programme autopsy: retroactive blind discovery on completed capital programmes, sold to reinsurers, lenders and sureties as underwriting calibration
Completed programmes have fully dated outcomes and no live political stakes, so access is easier than live-programme access
Discovery-as-diligence: model-space discovery for investment and credit committees, sold per-deal through fund networks
Committee-acknowledged decision-relevant findings missed by standard diligence in >= 50% of engagements
Make the measurement the product6 shapes

The hardest durable asset in the plan is the instrument, not the specialist: constructed worlds with hidden ground truth where regret and value of information are exactly computable. No conflict-free institution currently sells sealed evaluation, and no standard exists for synthetic-data fidelity or decision-quality scoring. These shapes monetise the measurement apparatus itself, to labs, enterprises and every producer of synthetic reasoning data.

Sealed decision-world benchmark suites with hidden ground truth, sold to labs and enterprises as the standard for scoring decision quality
2+ frontier labs or 3+ enterprises contract to evaluate against a Truna-built sealed suite within 3 quarters
Synthetic-corpus fidelity certification: audit third-party synthetic training data for realizer drift, sold to lab data-buying teams
3 paid audits from distinct lab or enterprise data teams within 12 months; 60% gross margin per audit
Decision-coverage certification: a neutral, probe-set-backed audit trail that a high-stakes decision was adversarially checked
10 decisions certified at >=$5k each within 2 pilot accounts; 100% backed by independently authored probe sets
Restructure the deal, not the company4 shapes

The proposed $15M round prices unresolved binary risk and passes ~$11.5M through to compute at venture dilution prices. These shapes apply the venture's own doctrine to its financing: buy the three kill experiments for $2-3M before pricing anything, split equity from brokered compute, and productise the gate structure itself as a repeatable instrument the fund can run on other hard-claim seeds.

A $2-3M pre-round instrument that buys the three kill experiments before anyone prices the company
All three kill experiments custodian-scored within 14 weeks of funding; conversion at a 25-40% effective discount if gates pass
Restructure the lead cheque: ~$6-8M equity plus a brokered compute syndicate replacing the ~$11.5M compute line
Equivalent GPU-hours secured for <= $7M effective cost; committed compute liability at month 9 under FAIL <= $1M
The evidence-priced seed franchise: the fund productises the kill-experiment pre-round as a repeatable deal structure
3 evidence-priced pre-rounds closed across the portfolio within 18 months; >= 60% of the apparatus reused deal-to-deal
Own the trust and custody layer4 shapes

The root fact under the thesis is that enterprises destroy their own decision reasoning for self-protection, and no institution exists to hold sealed evaluations, attest coverage or certify individual judgment. These shapes build the trust infrastructure the whole category needs: custody utilities, defensibility attestations bought from assurance budgets, safe decision-recording, and calibration credentials for the practitioners whose judgment feeds the system.

A neutral custody-and-succession utility for sealed AI evaluations, sold as a standard contract product to any AI vendor with capability claims
Five ownership structures no single institution currently sells, bundled into one standard contract product
An auditable 'nothing knowable was left unexamined' attestation for high-stakes commitments, recognised by the parties who adjudicate blame
1 coverage certificate formally tabled in a real capital-approval or board gate at a design partner within 9 months
Portable calibrated-judgment credential: backtest an expert's committed calls against dated recorded outcomes
50 experts outside the Truna panel pay for a calibration backtest within 6 months of offering

The cheapest ways to find out

Three tests that discriminate between the surviving families before committing real capital.

▶Run the retrieval context armInference plus one blind judging pass; two to three weeks

The completed comparison used worked examples taken from unrelated areas of work, the weakest form of context. Adding step-level retrieval of similar cases over the same 37 held-out cases, scored in one blind pass under the existing protocol, is a measurement one run answers. If retrieval closes the discriminating-quality gap the tuned model holds, the context-pack shape carries the value and the training spend is unnecessary; if it does not, training's 58% result stands.

▶Log one live discovery engagementOne nominated target, about four weeks, little cash beyond time

The fund nominates a discovery target and a founder-hour log runs alongside the machine for one complete engagement. This is the only observable route to the machine-run ratio; no public source contains it. It is a measurement, and it discriminates every service shape at once: context packs, the risk-register gap audit and the diligence product all require machine-run margins near 70%, while a low ratio reveals consulting economics that none of those shapes survives.

▶Double-grade a thousand accepted sequencesLow tens of thousands in panel fees; six to eight weeks

Independent experts regrade a random sample of sequences the verification pipeline has already accepted, measuring the false-accept rate directly. Published production data shows small specialist verifiers catching roughly one error in five, and in-loop verifier metrics reading five to ten times optimistic, so the answer is genuinely open. One run answers it — a measurement — and it gates the 100,000-sequence generation plan, the sealed-instrument shape and the $5.5M line before any training money is committed.

What this study does not establish

Volunteered rather than discovered, because the gaps change how much weight the rest carries.

  1. 73% of the 561 evidence items came back inconclusive, chiefly because the company's public footprint is a single page nineteen days old at the time of the work: founder identities, incorporation, contracts, panel terms, verifier design and budget decomposition all rest on the deck alone and were unverifiable from any independent source.
  2. Web search was rate-limited for long stretches of the run, so several lines of enquiry — GPU pricing trends, Indian procurement cycle times, expert-network reach into PSU staff — ended at blocked pages rather than answers.
  3. The searches for competing work used the phrase 'latent state', which returns state-space models rather than the latent reasoning and implicit chain-of-thought literature (Coconut, Quiet-STaR and related lines), so every claim about an unoccupied field is bounded by what was searched, not by what exists.
  4. The decomposition experiment settles the weights-versus-context question only in its weakest form: the step-level retrieval arm a sceptical reader would demand has not been run, no paired statistical tests are reported across the 37 cases, and a single judge scored everything.
  5. The number of experimental attempts the training and generation budgets are meant to buy was never disclosed, so whether the money is sufficient remains unpriced rather than answered.
  6. Of 247 venture shapes generated, 22 reached decision depth, and of 612 questions raised the majority remain open, most resolvable only through direct access to the founders, the design partners, or the fund's own records.

Q2Do trained weights beat the same material supplied as context?
Yes, on one step. The blind-scored decomposition experiment shows training closes 58% of the gap to a 27B reference against 32% from worked examples, and nothing matches the tuned model's empty-prompt 7.28. The retrieval arm is unrun.
88 evidence items · 265 items · 55 still open
Q3Does a trained-weights advantage survive frontier model releases?
No precedent. Zero documented cases of a fine-tuned capability holding commercial margin across three frontier releases; calibration does not survive base-model swaps, and retraining every two to four months is a recurring cost, not maintenance.
60 evidence items · 194 items · 29 still open
Q4Is the training and generation budget explained by disclosed cost drivers?
No. Both lines fund an unknown number of experimental attempts; base model size, adapters versus full fine-tuning, ablation count and GPU pricing basis are all undisclosed across a stated ten-fold range. No per-sequence figure is valid.
143 evidence items · 317 items · 59 still open
Q5What does the $11.5M compute line actually buy?
Unpriced. No pricing basis or quote date is stated anywhere; at three-year reserved rates the same capacity plausibly costs $4.6M-$6.9M, and reserved capacity is gated behind enterprise commitments a seed budget struggles to reach.
84 evidence items · 220 items · 38 still open
Q6Can the month 6-9 evidence programme execute on its own schedule?
Doubtful. No conflict-free custodian institution exists, no external body can ratify the metric inside six to ten weeks, panel grading runs on practitioner calendars, and verifier error rates are unmeasured at any scale.
124 evidence items · 298 items · 58 still open
Q7Is the competitive field genuinely unoccupied?
Bounded. Within what was searched, no published group combines the full thesis, but the searches missed the latent reasoning literature entirely (Coconut, Quiet-STaR), and adjacent simulation vendors such as Eon and Simile are already shipping.
145 evidence items · 289 items · 39 still open
Q8Should the round be priced now, or structured around the decisive tests?
Structured. A $2-3M pre-round funds the decisive work first: the verifier error curve as a one-run measurement, recipe work gated on progress across attempts, custodian-scored within 14 weeks and converting at a 25-40% discount on pass.

How this is organised. Everything sits in one of three sections, listed in the column on the leftunder Browse. Pick one and its contents fill this panel; click any row to go down a level. The trail at the top always shows where you are and takes you back. 1,165 of the 1,198 items have exactly one parent and nothing goes more than three levels deep, so it reads as an outline.

The maps. Any item can be switched to Map to see just its own neighbourhood — what it sits under, what it breaks into, and what links to it from elsewhere. The Map button in the left columnunder Browse instead shows the whole thing in three dimensions: either the 598 cross-links on their own, which is the part this outline cannot show, or all 1,198 items at once.

The other 598 connections do not follow the parent-child structure — they are things like one item feeding a risk into another (dependency 204 · causal 180 · risk_propagation 178 · control_mitigation 25 · financial_flow 11). They show as dashed gold lines on the map and as “feeds into / fed from” on the page.

Why the counts differ. The structure holds 1,198 items. The 247 venture shapes, 351 assumptions, 612 questions, 372 risks and 394 controls are not items — they sit alongside or hang off them, which is why a tag never finds them. Use the buttons above the tags to browse each set on its own.

Loose findings is a remainder, not a category: roots that never attached to the venture or to the outside world. Mostly scout signals that did not land under their parent, plus a few strays. It is named for what it is rather than dressed up as something coherent.

Tags versus groups. Tags are the exact kind the machine assigned (192 of them, so the long tail is behind “show all”). Groups bundle those into 13 broader buckets.

What is thin. 241 items have a written explanation; the other 957 are a headline only, because the run was stopped before every branch was written up.

Generated from the run's own output files by viz/build_dashboard.py (the narrative on the first two tabs comes from viz/build_study.py; the map coordinates from viz/layout3d.py). 192 distinct item types are grouped into 13 families for filtering; the exact type is shown on every item. The machine's own shorthand is translated on display and nothing else is edited: “the canvas” becomes “the plan”, the “[Scout]” tag is dropped while the source it names is kept, “UNKNOWN” becomes “open question”, and labels such as at_risk or fact_resolved are written out in words.
